organization: C-SPAN (Cable-Satellite Public Affairs Network) / C-SPAN Classroom
location: Online submission; no in-person event required
residency_requirement: None -- open to US and international students in the equivalent of grades 6-12
language_requirement: unknown -- not explicitly stated in the rules text retrieved. Verification note: check the full studentcam.org/rules/ page for an explicit language clause.
international_eligibility: Yes. Verbatim (official rules page): "International students in the equivalent of U.S. grades 6-12 and aged 18 years or younger may also participate."
turkiye_accessible: yes -- no country exclusion found; a Turkish student in grades 6-12 (or equivalent), aged 18 or younger, qualifies as an international entrant and would be judged in the 'High School-East' division (Europe/Africa bucket per the rules).
age_requirement: 18 years or younger for international entrants; U.S. entrants are grade-gated only
grade_requirement: U.S. grades 6-12 or international equivalent (Middle School 6-8, High School 9-12 divisions)
application_open: unknown exact open date; rules page live as of research date
program_dates: Documentary must be produced and uploaded by the Jan 20, 2027 deadline; runtime 5:00-6:00 minutes
cost_verbatim: No entry fee mentioned anywhere in the retrieved rules text.
prize_or_stipend: Cash prizes are awarded across categories; specific 2027 dollar amounts were not captured in this research pass (prizes page not fetched).
team_or_individual: Individual or team of up to 3 students. Verbatim: "Individuals or a team of up to 3 students may create and submit an entry." A student "may submit only one entry per year."
selection_process: Documentary must address the annual theme (current theme: "Mr. Speaker, I Rise To..." -- students produce a documentary on an issue they would raise in a first speech before the legislature). International entries are judged within separate regional divisions (Asia-Pacific / Europe & Africa / South & Central America) rather than against U.S. entries.
selectivity_evidence: No published acceptance rate found; this is a judged competition with regional divisions, not open enrollment.
required_documents: A single documentary video (5-6 minutes) plus a standard entry form; no separate essay.
verification_status: Critical eligibility fields (international/worldwide participation, grade/age, team size, documentary length, current deadline) verified verbatim from the official studentcam.org/rules/ page on 2026-08-29. Prize amounts and an explicit language policy were not independently confirmed this pass.
notes: Important cycle note: as of Aug 29, 2026 the live rules page shows theme "Mr. Speaker, I Rise To..." with a Jan 20, 2027 deadline -- this is the NEXT open cycle, since StudentCam 2026 winners were already announced earlier in 2026 (see studentcam.org/studentcam-2026-prize-winners/). Do not confuse this with the already-closed 2026 cycle.

organization: The English-Speaking Union (ESU), London -- delivered via national ESU branches / partner organisations (e.g. ESU Turkey)
delivery_mode: in_person (national heats in-country; international final in London)
location: National heats held in-country; international final at Dartmouth House, London, England
citizenship_requirement: None stated globally -- entry is via winning your country's ESU-affiliated national/regional competition, not a citizenship test.
residency_requirement: Must be a student in a country with an active ESU branch or ESU partner organisation running a qualifying national heat.
language_requirement: English. The competition is billed by ESU as "the Olympics of English public speaking."
international_eligibility: Yes, structurally: entry is via each country's own ESU-affiliated national heat rather than a direct individual application to London. Verbatim (esu.org): "this two-week tournament" [WSDC context aside] and, for IPSC specifically, participants are described as coming from "more than 40 countries" (esu.org) to "more than 50 countries" (secondary sourcing).
turkiye_accessible: yes -- ESU Turkey (English Speaking Union Turkey) runs an annual national IPSC final. Uskudar American Academy's own school news page states: "Our UAA'26 student Saba Koca won first place at the ESU International Public Speaking Competition (IPSC) national finals held at Hisar Schools on March 22nd!" and that the winner would advance to "the IPSC grand final in London." Multiple other Turkish schools' own sites (IELEV, Cevre Koleji, Sabanci University) independently corroborate a recurring Turkey national round in other years.
grade_requirement: unknown -- eligibility is age-based in sources checked, not grade-based
application_open: unknown -- set independently by each national ESU branch's own school-level heats, not centrally published
application_deadline: unknown for Turkey's specific 2026-2027 national heat timing
program_dates: IPSC programme 13-18 July 2026, London. Note: esu.org separately lists a "Finals Day" of "Monday, 1 June 2026" at Dartmouth House -- this date precedes the programme week and was not reconciled in this pass; it may refer to a related but distinct ESU public-speaking event.
cost: unknown for IPSC / for Turkey specifically
cost_verbatim: No IPSC-specific fee was found. (A separate ESU page about UK Team England/Wales debate selection -- a different competition, WSDC -- cites 'an individual registration fee of around $700' with means-tested bursaries; this figure must NOT be assumed to apply to IPSC.)
prize_or_stipend: Recognition as international final winner ("Olympics of English public speaking"); no cash prize amount confirmed in this pass.
selection_process: A student must first win their school/regional heat, then their national ESU-affiliated final, to become their country's sole representative at the London international final.
selectivity_evidence: Only one student per country advances to the London final; esu.org describes a base of "over 100,000 students from 50 countries" for ESU competitions generally. No other numeric rate published.
required_documents: None beyond winning the national round; ESU-style format typically includes a prepared speech and an impromptu/extempore element, not independently confirmed for the 2026-2027 IPSC rules in this pass.
official_application_url: unknown -- entry is through each country's national ESU branch (e.g. ESU Turkey), not a central online application
verification_status: Global structure, age range, language, and London final dates verified verbatim from esu.org. Turkey-specific accessibility was verified via a first-party Turkish school's own news page (referencing a 2024-cycle result) rather than ESU's own site, so this record is marked partially verified pending fresher ESU-sourced confirmation of Turkey's 2026-2027 national round.
notes: Distinguish from the World Schools Debating Championship (WSDC) -- also ESU-linked in some countries but a separate, team-based argumentative debate competition, recorded separately in this file as OEE-003.

organization: World Schools Debating Championships (independent international body, rotating annual host country); national teams are organized by each country's own debate federation (e.g. England/Wales team selection is run via the English-Speaking Union)
citizenship_requirement: Determined by each country's own national debate federation, not by WSDC centrally.
residency_requirement: Must be selected onto your country's official WSDC team by that country's national debate organizing body -- no direct individual entry exists.
international_eligibility: Structurally broad: verbatim (wsdcdebating.org): "The World Schools Debating Championships (WSDC) is a truly global competition for high school debaters. It is held annually and involves more than 70 national teams." Access for any individual student, however, depends entirely on whether their own country has an active, WSDC-recognized national team and selection process.
turkiye_accessible: unclear -- Turkey has hosted WSDC as a venue in a past year and has an active regional English-language debating scene (it hosts the separate, student-organized Eurasian Schools Debating Championship at Robert College, Istanbul), but no official source found in this pass confirms an active Turkish national team currently selects and fields debaters for WSDC. Genuine open question, not a confirmed exclusion.
age_requirement: 14-19 years old. Verbatim (esu.org, describing WSDC eligibility): "Age: 14-19."
grade_requirement: Secondary school enrollment required; no specific grade numbers published centrally
application_open: unknown centrally -- depends on each country's own federation timeline; UK's own trial process 'opens in late August each year' per esu.org (country-specific, not global)
currency: USD (UK example only, not confirmed general)
cost_verbatim: Verbatim (esu.org, describing Team England/Wales selection specifically, NOT a universal WSDC fee): "Individual registration fee of around $700; ESU means-tested bursaries are available. Trialling for the team is free of charge."
financial_aid: Means-tested bursaries confirmed for the UK national team specifically; unknown for other countries.
prize_or_stipend: Trophy/title recognition; no cash prize found.
selection_process: Each country's own national debate federation selects its team; format, timeline and rigor vary entirely by country. For England/Wales specifically: "Regional winners of the Schools' Mace and the Wales Schools Debating Championships will automatically be invited to trials upon application," with open applications also invited from "all competent debaters."
selectivity_evidence: One team represents each of 70+ countries; no numeric national-level acceptance rate published for any country's trials in sources checked.
required_documents: Determined by each country's own national selection process; unknown for Turkey specifically.
official_application_url: unknown -- no central application; UK-specific contact point is nationaldebateteam.org.uk
verification_status: Global scale, age range, and the 2026 host/dates were verified from wsdcdebating.org and esu.org directly. Turkey's specific national-team pathway is unresolved -- flagged as the single open item for a follow-up researcher to check directly with a Turkish debate federation or the WSDC organizing committee.
notes: Do not confuse with the Eurasian Schools Debating Championship (ESDC), a separate WSDC-FORMAT regional tournament physically hosted at Robert College, Istanbul, and already recorded elsewhere in ORYN's research (s6b_turkey_and_mixed_batch1.jsonl). Winning or attending ESDC is not the same as qualifying for a national WSDC team.

citizenship_requirement: None. Verbatim: "The Ayn Rand Institute's (ARI's) The Fountainhead essay contest is open to all students worldwide, except where void or prohibited by law."
language_requirement: English only. Verbatim: "Essays must be written in English only, and be between 800 and 1,600 words in length."
international_eligibility: Yes, explicitly worldwide per the rules text quoted above.
turkiye_accessible: yes -- no prohibition applicable to Turkey found; the worldwide eligibility clause has no geographic carve-out.
grade_requirement: Enrolled in grade 8, 9, 10, 11, or 12 during the contest school year. Verbatim: "Entrants must be at least 13 years of age and be enrolled as an 8th, 9th, 10th, 11th, or 12th student during the school year in which the contest is held. ARI reserves the right to make exceptions to this rule, on a case-by-case basis, for international students or for students with nonstandard school years."
application_deadline: UNRESOLVED. A secondary aggregator search result stated "June 7, 2026" for the current aynrand.org (US) cycle, but this could not be independently confirmed because the primary aynrand.org page is a JavaScript-rendered application that did not return readable content in this research pass. A rules mirror on the affiliated-but-legally-separate 'Ayn Rand Institute Canada' site shows a stale 'Next Entry Deadline: September 13, 2024' left over from a past cycle. Neither figure should be trusted as the confirmed current deadline without direct re-verification against aynrand.org.
cost_verbatim: No entry fee mentioned anywhere in the full rules text retrieved (via the ARI Canada mirror, which explicitly republishes ARI's rules).
prize_or_stipend: Per the ARI Canada rules mirror: Grand Prize $25,000 (1 winner), 1st Place $3,000 (2 winners), 2nd Place $2,000 (3 winners), 3rd Place $1,000 (3 winners). Not independently re-confirmed on the primary US site this pass, though the mirror explicitly presents these as ARI's own rules.
selection_process: "Essay submissions are evaluated in a fair and unbiased four-round judging process. Judges are individually selected by the Ayn Rand Institute based on a demonstrated knowledge and understanding of Ayn Rand's works." Judging is anonymized: "winners' names are unknown to judges until after essays have been ranked and the contest results finalized."
selectivity_evidence: No acceptance rate or entrant count published in sources checked.
required_documents: A single essay (800-1,600 words) responding to an assigned prompt about the novel The Fountainhead; essays must not include any personally identifying information.
essay_required: Yes -- the essay is the entire submission
official_application_url: https://aynrand.org/students/essay-contests/the-fountainhead (submission portal is linked from this page; the exact portal URL could not be captured because the page is JavaScript-rendered)
verification_status: Eligibility, age/grade, language, word count, fee-free status, and judging process were verified verbatim via the ARI Canada affiliate's rules mirror, which explicitly republishes 'ARI's' contest rules. The primary aynrand.org page could not be rendered directly (JavaScript single-page app blocked simple fetch tools), so the current-cycle deadline specifically is NOT independently confirmed and is flagged unknown rather than guessed.
notes: ARI runs a family of three essay contests (Anthem, The Fountainhead, Atlas Shrugged) at different grade bands; this record covers only The Fountainhead (grades 8-12), the band best matching ORYN's 14-18 age range. Do not silently assume the September 2024 deadline shown on the Canada mirror is current -- it is stale.

citizenship_requirement: None. Verbatim (official page): "Open to students in grades 9-12 worldwide."
residency_requirement: None stated; international students explicitly eligible.
language_requirement: English. Verbatim: "Entries must be submitted in English."
turkiye_accessible: yes -- no geographic exclusion found; worldwide grades 9-12 eligibility.
age_requirement: unknown exact age; eligibility is grade-based instead (see grade_requirement)
grade_requirement: Grades 9-12. Verbatim: "Students who have already graduated from high school are not eligible."
prize_or_stipend: First place $2,000; second place $1,000; third place $500; distinguished submissions $250 (per category: poetry, fiction, nonfiction). Secondary sources report Bennington College admission-scholarship consideration (up to full tuition) for finalists who separately apply to Bennington; this add-on benefit was not independently re-verified against the official cash-prize page in this pass.
selection_process: Submit one entry in one category only: poetry (up to 3 poems), fiction (one short story or standalone excerpt / one-act play), or nonfiction (personal or creative nonfiction essay or standalone excerpt) -- "Submissions must be 1500 words or less." Grades 9-11 submit via the Bennington YWA online portal; grade 12 submits via the Common Application or Coalition Application for Bennington College.
selectivity_evidence: No acceptance-rate or entrant-count published in the sources checked.
required_documents: One writing sample per the category rules above; no separate application essay or recommendation required.
essay_required: No separate application essay; the nonfiction category is itself an essay-form creative submission.
verification_status: All critical fields (grade eligibility, worldwide/international language, word limits, fee-free status, prize amounts, deadline) were verified verbatim from the official bennington.edu requirements-and-submissions page.
notes: Grade 12 applicants submit through a college-application platform (Common App / Coalition App) rather than the standalone YWA portal used by grades 9-11 -- a real mechanical difference worth flagging to students and families.

canonical_name: Quill and Scroll International Writing, Visual, Multimedia (WVM) Contest
organization: Quill and Scroll Society (headquartered in Minneapolis, MN; historically affiliated with the University of Iowa)
citizenship_requirement: None found explicitly; access is gated by the applicant's own school infrastructure (see notes), not by the student's citizenship.
residency_requirement: None stated for the student directly.
language_requirement: unknown -- not explicitly stated as English-only in the sections retrieved, though all categories and instructions are in English and assume a U.S.-style scholastic journalism program.
international_eligibility: Structurally gated rather than geographically restricted: entries must already be published work from a school-sponsored student publication (newspaper, yearbook, broadcast, online, etc.), submitted on the student's behalf by that school's journalism adviser -- not a direct individual application. Quill and Scroll's own promotional material (secondary-sourced) claims member schools 'in 44 countries' and the organization runs a distinct 'Quill and Scroll China' program, suggesting some non-U.S. participation exists.
turkiye_accessible: unclear -- no explicit country exclusion exists, but a Turkish student can only enter if their own school already runs a journalism program with an adviser willing to compile and submit the school's entries. No confirmed Turkish participating school was found in this pass.
age_requirement: unknown -- no explicit age stated; eligibility is grade-based instead
grade_requirement: Currently enrolled high school students (grades 9-12); separate Middle School Writing/Visual/Multimedia categories exist for younger students.
application_open: Open now. Verbatim: "2026 WVM is open for entries!"
application_deadline: February 6, 2026, midnight Central Time. Verbatim: "Entry deadline is Feb. 6 at midnight CT." NOTE: as of this research date (Aug 29, 2026) this specific deadline has already passed; the official page had not yet been updated to a 2027 cycle at time of checking.
program_dates: Eligible work must have been published between Feb. 6, 2025 and Feb. 5, 2026 (for the 2026 cycle).
cost_verbatim: "The fee for all entries is $8 for the 2026 contest."
prize_or_stipend: First/second/third place plus honorable mentions per category across 54 categories; an overall 'Blue and Gold Award' by class; award recipients become eligible to apply for Quill and Scroll student scholarships; News Writer of the Year winners become eligible for a $7,500 New York Times Summer Academy scholarship.
team_or_individual: Both -- most categories are individual entries; a few (e.g. In-Depth Reporting/Team Writing) explicitly allow multi-student team entries.
selection_process: Judges award 1st/2nd/3rd plus honorable mentions ("between 10 and 15 percent of all entries are recognized in every category") across 54 categories spanning writing, photography, design, video, audio and multimedia journalism.
selectivity_evidence: No overall acceptance rate published; the 10-15% honorable-mention figure is the only selectivity data given.
required_documents: Previously published work (a URL, PDF, or JPG of the published piece) -- the work must already be public, not written fresh for the contest.
recommendation_required: No formal recommendation, but a journalism adviser must compile and submit the entry on the student's behalf.
essay_required: No (varies by category: writing, photo, or multimedia work)
verification_status: Fee, deadline, published-work window, categories, and judging process were verified verbatim from the official quillandscroll.org contest page (fetched directly via HTTP request after the standard fetch tool was blocked). International/Turkey accessibility remains genuinely unresolved -- a real structural gap, not an oversight.
notes: This is fundamentally a SCHOOL-JOURNALISM-PROGRAM contest, not an individually-enterable competition: a student cannot submit directly and must have both (a) a published piece in a real school publication and (b) a cooperating journalism adviser to compile and submit entries via a shared spreadsheet naming the school and adviser. This is a meaningfully different access model from most other records in this file and should be surfaced clearly to students and parents.

organization: Columbia Scholastic Press Association (CSPA), housed at Columbia University School of Professional Studies
citizenship_requirement: None stated for the individual student.
residency_requirement: The student's own school must hold CSPA membership; if outside the US/Canada, the school must follow "an American plan of education."
language_requirement: unknown -- not explicitly stated in pages retrieved, but the program is built around English-language U.S.-style scholastic journalism.
international_eligibility: Conditional. Verbatim (CSPA's own about-CSPA page): "Students come from public, private and faith-based schools and colleges throughout the United States and from overseas schools which follow an American plan of education."
turkiye_accessible: unclear -- no Turkish member school was confirmed in this pass. A standard Turkish MEB-curriculum school, or a British-curriculum/IB-only school, would likely NOT qualify as following 'an American plan of education,' but a US-curriculum-accredited school operating in Turkey conceivably could. This needs direct confirmation against CSPA's member-school list, which was not accessible in this research pass.
age_requirement: unknown -- eligibility is publication-based, not individually age-gated
grade_requirement: Middle school, high school, and collegiate publications are all eligible; this record concerns the high-school-relevant tier.
application_open: unknown exact date for the current cycle
application_deadline: August 31, 2026 for work published in the 2025-2026 academic year, per a secondary aggregator (precollege.sps.columbia.edu-adjacent summary) -- NOT independently confirmed on an official CSPA deadlines page in this pass.
program_dates: Covers publications from the 2025-2026 academic year (per aggregator sourcing).
cost_verbatim: "A $55 membership fee is required for entry to CSPA awards programs." This is a school/publication membership fee, not a per-student or per-entry fee.
prize_or_stipend: Gold Circle Award recognition by category (News, Magazine, Digital Media, Yearbook); no cash prize identified.
team_or_individual: Individual student work is recognized, entered through the school's CSPA membership. Verbatim: "Gold Circle Awards are offered to recognize superior work by student journalists usually as individuals but sometimes as an entire staff."
selection_process: Entries are judged within the pool of CSPA member schools' submitted work, organized by major category.
selectivity_evidence: No acceptance-rate or entrant-count published in sources checked.
required_documents: Published student journalism work submitted under the school's CSPA membership.
recommendation_required: No formal recommendation, but requires an adviser/school to hold and use CSPA membership.
verification_status: The membership fee and the 'American plan of education' language for overseas schools were verified verbatim from official Columbia-hosted CSPA pages. The current-cycle deadline is aggregator-sourced only and not independently confirmed against an official CSPA page -- flagged accordingly. Whether any Turkish school currently holds CSPA membership was not resolved.
notes: Structural barrier distinct from citizenship: access requires (a) the student's own school to pay a $55/year CSPA membership, and (b) if the school is outside the US/Canada, that it follow 'an American plan of education' specifically -- a curriculum-type gate, not a nationality gate.

language_requirement: English (US-based literary competition; not independently re-verified as a standalone rule in the FAQ excerpt retrieved).
turkiye_accessible: no -- a Turkish citizen/resident student without US citizenship, a US green card, or independent US tax eligibility (SSN/ITIN) does not qualify. Recorded as a deliberate, well-documented exclusion because YoungArts is one of the most prestigious US teen writing competitions and ORYN users may ask about it by name.
application_deadline: Early October 2026 (search sources gave both Oct 6 and Oct 8, 2026 in different framings; not reconciled to a single verbatim date from a primary page in this pass -- verification note: check youngarts.org/apply directly if operationalized).
program_dates: National YoungArts Week is held in Miami for finalists; specific dates not captured in this pass.
cost: unknown -- not captured in this research pass. Verification note: check youngarts.org/apply for the current application fee and fee-waiver policy.
cost_verbatim: unknown -- not captured in this research pass.
financial_aid: Fee waivers are a well-known general program feature but were not independently verified with a verbatim quote in this pass.
prize_or_stipend: Cash awards and potential nomination as a U.S. Presidential Scholar in the Arts for top winners; not re-verified verbatim in this pass.
selection_process: Portfolio/manuscript submission judged by discipline; judging details were not verified beyond the eligibility gate in this pass.
selectivity_evidence: unknown -- no acceptance rate captured this pass.
required_documents: Writing portfolio/manuscript appropriate to the sub-discipline (Fiction, Nonfiction, Poetry, etc.)
essay_required: The submission itself is a writing sample, not a separate application essay.
verification_status: The citizenship/permanent-residency/taxable-income eligibility gate -- the critical field for this record -- was confirmed verbatim from the official youngarts.org FAQ page, including the explicit statement 'There are no exceptions to these guidelines.' citizenship_requirement: Not a citizenship test, but two compounding identity/residency gates (see residency_requirement).
residency_requirement: Verbatim (official FAQ): applicant must be "A resident of the United States (continental U.S., Alaska, or Hawaii)" and must "identify as Jewish"; project leadership must also be "conducted from the U.S., though projects may have global reach."
language_requirement: unknown -- not captured; presumed English given US-only scope.
turkiye_accessible: no -- excluded on residency grounds alone, independent of the separate Jewish-identity requirement. Recorded as a deliberate exclusion given how well-known this award is within Jewish youth-leadership circles.
age_requirement: 15-19 years old by the application deadline
application_deadline: January 8, 2026 (2026 cycle; already closed as of this research date)
cost_verbatim: unknown -- not explicitly captured; Diller awards are not known to charge an application fee. Verification note: confirm on dillerteenawards.org/apply directly.
prize_or_stipend: unknown exact amount this pass; historically a cash award plus a leadership retreat, per general program reputation -- not re-verified verbatim.
team_or_individual: individual (co-led projects: "no more than one applicant per project will be chosen as an award recipient")
selection_process: Applicant must be currently serving, unpaid, in a leadership role on a service project (Jewish community or broader community). Siblings of a recent (within 5 years) award recipient are ineligible.
required_documents: unknown in detail -- application form describing the applicant's leadership role and project.
verification_status: The two critical exclusion gates (Jewish identity and US residency, including that project leadership itself must be conducted from the U.S.) were confirmed verbatim from the official dillerteenawards.org FAQ page.
notes: DELIBERATE EXCLUSION RECORD. Two independent, compounding barriers exist: (1) must 'identify as Jewish,' and (2) must be a US resident with project leadership 'conducted from the U.S.' Either alone would exclude the great majority of ORYN's Turkiye-based users; both together make this unambiguous.

canonical_name: Three Dot Dash: Global Teen Leader (GTL) Program
delivery_mode: online_application; in-person summit for selected Global Teen Leaders
location: Online application; summit location varies by year (a recent cycle was held in Stockholm; a 2026 'Just Peace Summit' in London was referenced by a secondary aggregator but not independently confirmed on the primary site this pass)
language_requirement: unknown -- application appears to be in English; not explicitly stated as a rule in pages retrieved.
international_eligibility: Claimed broad global reach. Verbatim (official site): "Our GTLs come from 75+ countries on 6 continents." This describes past outcomes rather than a stated eligibility rule, and no explicit country exclusion was found.
turkiye_accessible: unclear -- no country exclusion found and the program claims broad global reach, but no Turkish Global Teen Leader was specifically identified in sources checked. The environmental-project and nominator-reference requirements are the operative gates, not geography.
age_requirement: 13-19 years old in the application year. Verbatim (official pre-application eligibility question, 2025 cycle): "Will I be 13-19 years old in 2025?"
application_open: unknown for the next cycle; most recently confirmed: 2025-cycle Pre-Application opened before January 26, 2025
application_deadline: unknown for the next cycle. Most recently confirmed from the official site (2025 cycle, now archived): Pre-Application due January 26, 2025; Main Application due February 2, 2025. A secondary aggregator (opportunitydesk.org, not independently confirmed against an official page) separately reported a 2026-cycle deadline of March 26, 2026, which has already passed as of this research date.
program_dates: Summit dates vary by year; not independently confirmed for the next cycle in this pass.
cost_verbatim: Official site, in response to a cost question: "Absolutely not" -- there is no cost to apply or attend; for the archived 2025/Stockholm cycle specifically: "all air/train travel, visa fees, hotel, meals, and ground travel in Stockholm will be paid for by We Are Family Foundation."
financial_aid: Full program-funded travel, visa fees, accommodation and meals for selected Global Teen Leaders.
prize_or_stipend: Selection as a 'Global Teen Leader' plus a funded trip to the annual summit, a yearlong mentorship, and ongoing access to WAFF's leadership network and virtual programming.
selection_process: Three steps: (1) Pre-Application self-screened against seven yes/no eligibility questions (age, active and already-impactful work, environmental focus, personal leadership role, demonstrable impact, and a 2-year continuation plan), reviewed by WAFF's Internal Selection Committee within about a week; (2) Main Application (20-30 minutes) if pre-approved; (3) a required 'Nominator' -- a reference from an Educator, a WAFF Alumni, a Coalition Partner, a WAFF Team Member, or a 'Community Champion' who personally knows the applicant's work and is explicitly NOT a relative or close friend -- submits a recommendation as part of the Main Application.
selectivity_evidence: No numeric acceptance rate published; described only as identifying and curating a cohort of Global Teen Leaders annually.
required_documents: Pre-Application, Main Application, and one Nominator reference/recommendation.
recommendation_required: Yes -- a Nominator reference is a required part of the Main Application (see selection_process).
essay_required: unknown in exact format, but the Main Application requires substantive written responses about the applicant's project and impact.

language_requirement: English (spoken/discussion-based ethics case competition; not explicitly restated as a standalone rule in pages retrieved).
turkiye_accessible: unclear -- Turkey is geographically transcontinental (partly in Europe), so it is genuinely ambiguous whether TKEthics' 'European/UK school based teams' framing would include a Turkish school. prize_or_stipend: unknown -- not captured this pass; appears to be recognition-based (regional qualifier feeding an 'International Ethics Olympiad' final) rather than cash-prize based.

This direct contradiction between two time points is reported honestly rather than resolved by assumption -- hence LEAD tier rather than PARTIALLY_VERIFIED, since the unresolved item is eligibility itself, not just a logistics detail.

international_eligibility: No -- restricted to accredited U.S. high schools; teams must compete in the in-state/regional bowl closest to their school.
